# Policies, thresholds and constants

All numeric policy values of methodology 0.1.0, read directly from `src/openfactsheet/policy/defaults.py` and `src/openfactsheet/policy/thresholds.py`. They are conventions, versioned with the methodology and never tuned per fund. The rules that use them are described in [criteria](criteria.md).

## Minimum-data policies

Below the mathematical minimum a metric is `insufficient_data`; the statistical thresholds set the base confidence (low / moderate / high).

| Policy | Mathematical minimum | Basis | Low below | Moderate below | Metrics |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `observed_point` | 1 obs | none (always high) | — | — | `cumulative_return`, `best_period`, `worst_period`, `current_drawdown`, `zero_return_pct` |
| `path_risk` | 1 obs | years of history | 3 | 5 | `max_drawdown`, `average_drawdown`, `longest_drawdown_duration`, `drawdown_count`, `time_underwater_pct`, `ulcer_index`, `pain_index`, `median_drawdown`, `average_drawdown_duration`, `max_peak_to_trough_duration`, `average_recovery_duration`, `longest_winning_streak`, `longest_losing_streak`, `best_calendar_year`, `worst_calendar_year`, `positive_calendar_years_pct`, `best_rolling_year`, `worst_rolling_year`, `positive_rolling_year_pct` |
| `location` | 1 obs | years of history | 3 | 5 | `cagr`, `arithmetic_mean`, `geometric_mean_return`, `annualized_arithmetic_mean`, `median_return`, `positive_period_pct`, `negative_period_pct` |
| `dispersion` | 2 obs | years of history | 3 | 5 | `volatility`, `annualized_volatility`, `mean_absolute_deviation`, `interquartile_range`, `downside_deviation`, `semi_deviation`, `downside_potential`, `gaussian_var_95`, `mean_return_standard_error` |
| `ratio_standard` | 2 obs | years of history | 3 | 5 | `gain_to_pain_ratio`, `payoff_ratio`, `profit_factor`, `sharpe_ratio`, `sortino_ratio`, `calmar_ratio`, `martin_ratio`, `omega_ratio`, `kappa_3_ratio`, `upside_potential_ratio`, `burke_ratio`, `sterling_ratio`, `pain_ratio`, `recovery_factor` |
| `skewness` | 3 obs | observations | 60 | 120 | `skewness`, `jarque_bera_pvalue` |
| `kurtosis` | 4 obs | observations | 120 | 240 | `modified_var_95`, `modified_es_95`, `excess_kurtosis` |
| `tail` | 2 obs | expected tail observations | 5 | 10 | `drawdown_at_risk_95`, `cdar_95`, `edar_95`, `var_historical_95`, `expected_shortfall_historical_95`, `tail_ratio`, `evar_95` |
| `autocorrelation` | 5 obs | observations | 36 | 60 | `autocorrelation_lag1`, `autocorrelation_lag2`, `autocorrelation_lag3` |
| `ljung_box` | 10 obs | observations | 36 | 60 | `ljung_box_pvalue` |
| `asymptotic_inference` | 4 obs | observations | 36 | 60 | `probabilistic_sharpe_ratio`, `sharpe_ratio_standard_error`, `minimum_track_record_length` |
| `benchmark_regression` | 3 obs | years of history | 3 | 5 | `beta`, `alpha`, `r_squared`, `correlation`, `treynor_ratio`, `residual_volatility`, `appraisal_ratio`, `bull_beta`, `bear_beta`, `timing_ratio` |
| `benchmark_simple` | 2 obs | years of history | 3 | 5 | `tracking_error`, `active_return`, `information_ratio`, `upside_capture`, `downside_capture`, `capture_ratio`, `batting_average`, `m_squared` |
| `long_horizon_dependence` | 4 obs | years of history | 5 | 10 | `sharpe_ratio_autocorrelation_adjusted`, `variance_ratio_1y` |
| `factor_regression` | 3 obs | years of history | 3 | 5 | `factor_alpha`, `factor_alpha_t_statistic`, `factor_r_squared`, `factor_residual_volatility` |

Policy descriptions:

- `observed_point`: Observed fact about the supplied history; any non-empty history suffices.
- `path_risk`: Path statistics (drawdowns, streaks) are computable from one observation but are unrepresentative below 3 years (low) and 5 years (moderate); longer histories tend to reveal deeper drawdowns.
- `location`: Mean-type estimates: low confidence below 3 years, moderate below 5 years.
- `dispersion`: Requires at least 2 observations; low confidence below 3 years, moderate below 5.
- `ratio_standard`: Risk-adjusted ratios: at least 2 observations; low confidence below 3 years, moderate below 5 years.
- `skewness`: Requires at least 3 observations; standard error is roughly sqrt(6/n), so low confidence below 60 and moderate below 120 observations.
- `kurtosis`: Requires at least 4 observations; kurtosis estimates are highly unstable, so low confidence below 120 and moderate below 240 observations.
- `tail`: Requires at least 2 observations; low confidence when fewer than 5 observations are expected in the 5% tail (n < 100), moderate when fewer than 10 (n < 200).
- `autocorrelation`: Requires at least 5 observations; standard error is roughly 1/sqrt(n), so low confidence below 36 and moderate below 60 observations.
- `ljung_box`: Requires at least 10 observations for a 3-lag test; low below 36, moderate below 60.
- `asymptotic_inference`: Asymptotic Sharpe-ratio inference needs at least 4 observations for the moments it uses; the normal approximation is poor below 36 observations (low) and 60 (moderate).
- `benchmark_regression`: Requires at least 3 aligned observations; low confidence below 3 years of overlap, moderate below 5 years.
- `benchmark_simple`: Requires at least 2 aligned observations; low confidence below 3 years of overlap, moderate below 5 years.
- `long_horizon_dependence`: One-year-horizon serial-correlation statistics need at least two years of data (undefined below); their standard error is about sqrt(4 / (3 y)) for y years, so confidence is low below 5 years and moderate below 10 years.
- `factor_regression`: Requires at least 3 aligned observations and at least k + 2 for k factors (k + 1 coefficients and one residual degree of freedom); low confidence below 3 years of overlap, moderate below 5 years.

## Annualization factors

| Frequency | Periods per year P |
|---|---|
| daily business | 252 |
| daily calendar | 365 |
| weekly | 52 |
| monthly | 12 |
| quarterly | 4 |
| yearly | 1 |

Irregular: not annualized. Unknown: not annualized unless the caller declares the observation frequency. Scaling: square-root-of-time for volatility; linear for arithmetic means.

## Return-scale classifier bounds

A series is confidently decimal when its median absolute non-zero value is at most `upper / divisor`; percent when it exceeds `upper`; the zone in between is ambiguous (percent only if some value is below -1, otherwise the caller must declare the scale).

Confident divisor: 4.

| Frequency | Decimal upper bound | Confident-decimal bound |
|---|---|---|
| daily | 0.05 | 0.0125 |
| weekly | 0.1 | 0.025 |
| monthly | 0.2 | 0.05 |
| quarterly | 0.3 | 0.075 |
| yearly | 0.6 | 0.15 |
| irregular | 0.3 | 0.075 |
| unknown | 0.3 | 0.075 |

## Diagnostic and confidence thresholds

| Rule | Value | Source key |
|---|---|---|
| Smoothing risk assessed from | 12 observations | `smoothing.min_observations` |
| High smoothing risk | rho_1 >= 0.3 and z >= 1.96 | `smoothing.high` |
| Moderate smoothing risk | rho_1 >= 0.15 and z >= 1.645 | `smoothing.moderate` |
| Excessive zero returns | share >= 10% | `stale_returns.zero_share_warning` |
| Repeated returns | run >= 3 identical values | `stale_returns.identical_run_warning` |
| Suspicious large return | robust z > 5 | `outliers.robust_z_threshold` |
| Distribution-shape warning | n >= 24, skewness <= -1 or excess kurtosis >= 3 | `distribution_warning` |
| Ljung-Box lags | 3 | `dependence.ljung_box_lags` |
| Benchmark coverage cap | overlap < 90% of fund observations → at most moderate | `confidence.benchmark_min_coverage` |
| Factor coverage cap | overlap < 90% of fund observations → at most moderate | `confidence.factor_min_coverage` |
| Short annualization | years < 1 → low | `confidence.annualization_min_years` |

This is the `methodology` object embedded in every JSON report.

```json
{
  "conventions": {
    "annual_return": {
      "description": "geometric (CAGR): (prod(1 + r))^(periods_per_year / n) - 1; the arithmetic mean x periods_per_year is reported separately",
      "method": "geometric"
    },
    "annualization": {
      "irregular": "not annualized",
      "periods_per_year": {
        "daily_business": 252.0,
        "daily_calendar": 365.0,
        "monthly": 12.0,
        "quarterly": 4.0,
        "weekly": 52.0,
        "yearly": 1.0
      },
      "scaling": "square-root-of-time for volatility; linear for arithmetic means",
      "unknown": "not annualized unless the caller declares the observation frequency"
    },
    "benchmark": {
      "alignment": "intersection of periods; never filled",
      "alpha_annualization": "arithmetic: per-period intercept x periods_per_year",
      "appraisal_ratio": "annualized OLS alpha / annualized residual volatility",
      "batting_average": "share of aligned periods with fund return strictly above benchmark",
      "capture": "geometric, annualized over up (benchmark > 0) or down (benchmark < 0) periods",
      "capture_ratio": "upside capture / downside capture; undefined unless downside capture > 0",
      "description": "periods aligned on their intersection (monthly/quarterly/yearly by calendar period, daily/weekly by exact date); missing benchmark returns are never filled",
      "information_ratio": "annualized arithmetic mean active return / tracking error",
      "m_squared": "aligned Sharpe ratio x benchmark volatility, arithmetic annualization",
      "regime_betas": "OLS with intercept on benchmark > 0 (bull) or < 0 (bear) periods",
      "regression": "OLS of fund on benchmark returns (risk-free = 0)",
      "residual_volatility": "OLS regression standard error (m - 2 dof) x sqrt(periods_per_year)",
      "timing_ratio": "bull beta / bear beta; undefined unless bear beta > 0"

    "calendar_years": {
      "daily_weekly_edge_tolerance_days": 7,
      "monthly": "all 12 calendar months observed",
      "quarterly": "all 4 calendar quarters observed",
      "yearly": "the year's observation"
    },
    "charts": {
```
